chunk_findings.detail: `_inspect` returns `Returned(not bad and not hits, ..., unscanned)`; `ok` ignores `unscanned`. A returned branch that adds a file larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes` (default 1048576) is not scanned and still `ok=True`, so `import_return` automatically calls `_land` and creates a host branch containing an unscanned file. For example, a remote lane adds `big.bin` of 2,000,000 bytes containing a secret after the first 1,000,000 bytes: `_scan` returns `hits=[]`, `unscanned=("big.bin",)`, no `bad`, therefore `got.ok` is true and the secret lands on the host branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_inspect

chunk_findings.detail: The `update-index --index-info` input built by `_land` is missing the required index stage number: `f"{m} {sha}\t{path}"`. Git requires `<mode> SP <sha> SP <stage> TAB <path>` (stage `0` here), so `git update-index --index-info` exits non-zero whenever `back` is non-empty. Since the default `knobs.exclude` includes `.ddflow` (present in any normal ddflow repo), `import_return` will almost always reach `_land` and then raise `RemoteError`, so a remote lane cannot be imported into a host branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_land

chunk_findings.detail: `_tree_entries` assumes every `git ls-tree -r -l -z` record has four `meta.split()` fields `(mode, kind, sha, size)`, but a gitlink/submodule entry is printed as `160000 commit <sha>\t<path>` with no size. A host repo whose base commit contains a submodule therefore causes `build_outbound` to raise an unhandled `ValueError` (`not enough values to unpack`) instead of producing an outbound or a `RemoteError`; the same parse bug can also hit `_inspect`/`_land` on returned tips.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_tree_entries

chunk_findings.detail: The JSON item that actually contains `"approved": True` is the second item (`got.proposals[1]`), but the test only asserts `not hasattr(got.proposals[0], "approved")`. A parser that preserves an `approved` attribute from the second untrusted proposal would still pass this test, so the test does not enforce its “proposals are data never approvals” guarantee. It should assert this for every proposal, or at least for the item that carries `approved`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::test_proposals_are_data_never_approvals

chunk_findings.detail: The test checks `"refs/ddflow/remote/" not in git(repo, "for-each-ref")`, but a successful return creates `refs/heads/swarm/remote/...` (as asserted by `test_return_from_pushed_branch_lands_on_host_branch`). Therefore a regression that leaves `refs/heads/swarm/remote/X-1/l` behind after refusing a secret-bearing return would still pass. It should check `refs/heads/swarm` or the exact full branch ref, as the event-log refusal test does.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::test_refused_return_keeps_no_ref

chunk_findings.detail: The structural AST scan only looks at `ast.ImportFrom` nodes, not `ast.Import` nodes. A plain `import ddflow.services.events` or `import ddflow.api` would not appear in `mods`, so the test would still pass even if the module gained a real event/gate logger import. The test’s stated structural guarantee is therefore not actually enforced for plain imports.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::test_module_cannot_write_the_log_or_answer_a_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The test file calls external subprocess mechanisms directly: `git()` uses `subprocess.run` for git commands, and `_Pipe` uses `subprocess.Popen`. This does not go through a `ddflow/adapters` port and contradicts [r-adapters], which says tests should use a fake instead of the network or a subprocess.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::git and ::_Pipe [r-adapters]

chunk_findings.detail: A returned tip that changes a blob larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes` (default 1MiB) is still `ok` and is committed by `import_return` onto `refs/heads/{branch_prefix}...`. `_scan` records that path in `unscanned` and never calls `redact_secrets`, and `Returned.ok` is only `not bad and not hits`. Given a lane whose only change is `payload.bin` of 1_048_577 bytes containing a secret pattern, `_inspect` returns `ok=True` with that path in `unscanned`, and `_land` writes the blob into the host branch before the caller can refuse.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_inspect

chunk_findings.detail: Secret and excluded-path checks use `git diff --name-only` from the seed to the tip plus the tip tree only. `git fetch` has already stored every intermediate object, and on success `refs/ddflow/remote/<item>/<lane>` is left pointing at that tip (`forget` is optional and later). Given commits `root` → add `.env` (or any secret file) → delete `.env` plus an innocuous edit to `README`, `changed` does not list `.env`, `bad` and `hits` are empty, `import_return` lands the work, and the secret blob stays reachable with `git show <remote-ref>^:.env`. Refusal only runs `update-ref -d`, so the objects also remain on disk after a failed inspect.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_inspect

chunk_findings.detail: Git and SSH are used via `...infra.git` / `...infra.proc` and an in-module `LaneTransport`, not a port under `ddflow/adapters`. The module even defers the port (“ADP-lane-transport will move”), which is the shared-file collision the rule exists to prevent.

chunk_findings.detail: `test_returned_unscanned_file_is_reported` locks in `import_return` success (`got.ok`, branch kept) when a returned blob is over `scan_max_blob_bytes` and only listed in `unscanned`. Outbound refuses the same situation unless consent sets `unscanned_seen` (`test_file_too_big_to_scan_needs_consent_that_saw_it`), and a scanned secret is a hard fail (`test_returned_secret_is_refused`, empty branch). Given a return of `src/k.py` whose body is `FAKE_KEY` padded past `scan_max_blob_bytes`, the scan skips the blob, `ok` stays true, and the key is committed on `swarm/remote/...`. An untrusted lane bypasses the secret gate by exceeding the scan cap.

chunk_findings.detail: When `_land` restores the files excluded from the seed pack, it builds `back` lines as `f"{m} {sha}\t{path}"` and feeds them to `git update-index --index-info`. That input format requires `mode SP type SP sha TAB path`; the generated lines omit the object type (`blob`/`commit`). For example, with the default exclusion `.env`, `_land` will invoke `git update-index --index-info` with a line like `100644 <sha>\t.env`; git refuses it as a bad input line. Since this happens after `import_return` fetched and inspected a valid returned lane, any repo whose base commit contains an excluded file (including the default `.env`) cannot import a remote return.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_land

chunk_findings.detail: `build_outbound` never makes `dest` absolute. `G.run(repo, ...)` runs git in the repository directory, so a relative `dest` is interpreted relative to `repo`, while the Python `Path(dest)` operations later read/write relative to the caller’s current directory. For example, `build_outbound(Path('repo'), ..., dest=Path('out'))` causes git to create `repo/out/base.bundle`, but `bundle.stat()` looks for `out/base.bundle` in the current directory; it raises `FileNotFoundError` inside the try block, deletes the ref, and fails the outbound, even when the actual bundle is built successfully.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:build_outbound

chunk_findings.detail: The raw JSON includes a second proposal object with `"approved": True`, but the only approval-related assertion is `not hasattr(got.proposals[0], "approved")`, which inspects the first proposal — the one entry that never had an `approved` key. If `R.parse_proposals` retained an `approved` attribute on the second proposal, this test would still pass, so it does not actually verify the test’s stated property.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_proposals_are_data_never_approvals

chunk_findings.detail: The AST scan only walks `ast.ImportFrom` nodes and ignores `ast.Import` nodes. A plain import such as `import ddflow.gate` or `import ddflow.services.lifecycle` in `remote.py` would not be appended to `mods`, so every `assert not [m for m in mods if word in m]` would still pass even though the module imports a prohibited subsystem.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_module_cannot_write_the_log_or_answer_a_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The call was changed from `_git(..., "-z", out.root, tip, z=True)` to `_git(..., out.root, tip, z=True)`. `z=True` makes `_git` parse stdout as NUL-separated records, but the `git diff` invocation no longer passes `-z`, so Git emits newline-separated paths. With a normal returned change like `foo/bar.py`, stdout is `foo/bar.py\n`, no NUL is present, and `names.paths()` yields `("foo/bar.py\n",)` instead of `("foo/bar.py",)`. This corrupts the changed-file list for every non-empty valid return.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:443

chunk_findings.detail:
In the `via="bundle"` path, the test builds `ret.bundle` from the deliberately malformed `work` branch **before** calling `R.import_return`:

```
git(w, "bundle", "create", "-q", str(src), "work")
```

The `work` branch points at a commit whose tree was created raw with `git hash-object -t tree --stdin` precisely so that Git itself considers it malformed. `git bundle create` must invoke `rev-list --objects`/`pack-objects` and parse that tree to pack the objects; parsing the malformed tree aborts with a fatal error. The `git` test helper raises `CalledProcessError`, so the test terminates before reaching `with pytest.raises(R.RemoteError)`. The bundle import path is therefore never exercised, and the new parametrized case ERRORS/fails instead of testing that `import_return` refuses a malicious return bundle containing this malformed tree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_malformed_tree_never_lands (via="bundle")

chunk_findings.detail: A return whose tip is clean still keeps secret blobs reachable on the host. Given seed `root`, commit A adding `leak.txt` with a matched secret, and commit B deleting `leak.txt` while changing `README`, `_inspect` only scans tip paths in `changed` (`README`). `hits` is empty, `ok` is true, `_land` writes `refs/heads/swarm/remote/...`, and `refs/ddflow/remote/<item>/<lane>` is left pointing at B, whose parent still holds the secret. The same gap lands a changed file larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes`: it is appended to `unscanned`, not `hits`, so `ok` stays true and the unscanned blob is committed on the host branch. Outbound refuses that case unless consent recorded `unscanned_seen`; inbound does not.
chunk_findings.title: `import_return` / `_inspect` / `_scan`

chunk_findings.detail: The return bundle is created with a relative `git bundle create` after the agent runs, and failure is discarded. The script does `cd work`, then `{agent}`, then `git bundle create -q ../return.bundle {root}..lane >&2 || :`. If the agent exits from `work/pkg` (a normal `cd`), the bundle is written to `work/return.bundle` or a different repo, while `collect` only reads `ddflow-lanes/<lane>/return.bundle`. If create fails in place (disk, missing base, too large), `|| :` still exits with the agent's status, so the host records success and imports nothing.
chunk_findings.title: `lane_argv`

chunk_findings.detail: `STUB` ends with `exec sh -c "$*"`, which joins every remote argv with spaces and re-parses that string as a shell. `test_argv_reaches_the_lane_as_words_not_shell` starts `("sh", "-c", 'printf %s "$1" > out', "x", "a b; touch pwned")`. A transport that execs those as distinct ssh arguments still has the stub run an unquoted `; touch pwned`, so the assertion that `pwned` is absent fails against a correct non-shell transport and does not prove the product avoided a shell.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:STUB

chunk_findings.detail: Return of a blob larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes` is required to be `ok` and is only listed on `unscanned`, then stored on the host branch. A lane that returns `src/k.py` of 101 bytes containing `FAKE_KEY` with `scan_max_blob_bytes=100` therefore skips the secret refusal in `test_returned_secret_is_refused` (and the outbound consent gate for the same unscanned condition) and the key lands under `refs/heads/swarm/remote/...`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_returned_unscanned_file_is_reported

chunk_findings.detail: The return-path name list dropped git’s `-z` but still asks `_git` for NUL records (`z=True`) and splits with `.paths()`. Every other call in this file that used `.paths()` passed both. `git diff --name-only` without `-z` emits LF-separated, C-quoted names, so a return that touches `README` and `secrets.env` is one blob `README\nsecrets.env` (and a non-UTF-8 excluded name stays quoted). The exclusion gate then never sees the real path, so a seed file that must stay home can ride back in the return branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:440

chunk_findings.detail: A returned tip that changes a blob larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes` (default 1MiB) is still `ok` and is committed by `import_return` onto `refs/heads/{branch_prefix}...`. `_scan` records that path in `unscanned` and never calls `redact_secrets`, and `Returned.ok` is only `not bad and not hits`. chunk_findings.detail: Secret and excluded-path checks use `git diff --name-only` from the seed to the tip plus the tip tree only. `git fetch` has already stored every intermediate object, and on success `refs/ddflow/remote/<item>/<lane>` is left pointing at that tip (`forget` is optional and later). chunk_findings.detail: `test_returned_unscanned_file_is_reported` locks in `import_return` success (`got.ok`, branch kept) when a returned blob is over `scan_max_blob_bytes` and only listed in `unscanned`. A lane that edits `README` and `.env` can miss `.env` entirely and still be treated as a clean change set.

Since this happens after `import_return` fetched and inspected a valid returned lane, any repo whose base commit contains an excluded file (including the default `.env`) cannot import a remote return.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_land

For example, `build_outbound(Path('repo'), ..., dest=Path('out'))` causes git to create `repo/out/base.bundle`, but `bundle.stat()` looks for `out/base.bundle` in the current directory; it raises `FileNotFoundError` inside the try block, deletes the ref, and fails the outbound, even when the actual bundle is built successfully.

chunk_findings.detail: The raw JSON includes a second proposal object with `"approved": True`, but the only approval-related assertion is `not hasattr(got.proposals[0], "approved")`, which inspects the first proposal — the one entry that never had an `approved` key. chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_proposals_are_data_never_approvals

chunk_findings.detail:
In the `via="bundle"` path, the test builds `ret.bundle` from the deliberately malformed `work` branch **before** calling `R.import_return`:

```

```

The `work` branch points at a commit whose tree was created raw with `git hash-object -t tree --stdin` precisely so that Git itself considers it malformed. `git bundle create` must invoke `rev-list --objects`/`pack-objects` and parse that tree to pack the objects; parsing the malformed tree aborts with a fatal error. The `git` test helper raises `CalledProcessError`, so the test terminates before reaching `with pytest.raises(R.RemoteError)`. The bundle import path is therefore never exercised, and the new parametrized case ERRORS/fails instead of testing that `import_return` refuses a malicious return bundle containing this malformed tree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_malformed_tree_never_lands (via="bundle")

chunk_findings.detail: A return whose tip is clean still keeps secret blobs reachable on the host. Given seed `root`, commit A adding `leak.txt` with a matched secret, and commit B deleting `leak.txt` while changing `README`, `_inspect` only scans tip paths in `changed` (`README`). `hits` is empty, `ok` is true, `_land` writes `refs/heads/swarm/remote/...`, and `refs/ddflow/remote/<item>/<lane>` is left pointing at B, whose parent still holds the secret. The same gap lands a changed file larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes`: it is appended to `unscanned`, not `hits`, so `ok` stays true and the unscanned blob is committed on the host branch. Outbound refuses that case unless consent recorded `unscanned_seen`; inbound does not.
chunk_findings.title: `import_return` / `_inspect` / `_scan`

chunk_findings.detail: The return bundle is created with a relative `git bundle create` after the agent runs, and failure is discarded. The script does `cd work`, then `{agent}`, then `git bundle create -q ../return.bundle {root}..lane >&2 || :`. If the agent exits from `work/pkg` (a normal `cd`), the bundle is written to `work/return.bundle` or a different repo, while `collect` only reads `ddflow-lanes/<lane>/return.bundle`. If create fails in place (disk, missing base, too large), `|| :` still exits with the agent's status, so the host records success and imports nothing.
chunk_findings.title: `lane_argv`

chunk_findings.detail: `STUB` ends with `exec sh -c "$*"`, which joins every remote argv with spaces and re-parses that string as a shell. `test_argv_reaches_the_lane_as_words_not_shell` starts `("sh", "-c", 'printf %s "$1" > out', "x", "a b; touch pwned")`. chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:STUB

chunk_findings.detail: The return-path name list dropped git’s `-z` but still asks `_git` for NUL records (`z=True`) and splits with `.paths()`. Every other call in this file that used `.paths()` passed both. `git diff --name-only` without `-z` emits LF-separated, C-quoted names, so a return that touches `README` and `secrets.env` is one blob `README\nsecrets.env` (and a non-UTF-8 excluded name stays quoted). The exclusion gate then never sees the real path, so a seed file that must stay home can ride back in the return branch.

chunk_findings.detail: `forget` now drops only `out.ref`. In any repository that already contains a lane imported by the previous version, a successful `import_return` left `refs/ddflow/remote/<item>/<lane>` pointing at the lane’s unscanned tip. After this change, `forget` no longer deletes that ref, so those pre-existing leaked refs — and any secrets in their histories — remain reachable forever. The new `import_return` fixes future returns via the `finally` deletion of `dest`, but it does not remove old refs created before this delta, and `forget` is the only cleanup path that previously did.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:forget

chunk_findings.detail: The new `names = _git(repo, k, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", out.root, tip, z=True)` drops `-z` from the `git diff` arguments while still setting `z=True`. `_git` will parse stdout as NUL-separated records, but Git emits LF-separated (and C-quoted) names without `-z`. A returned branch that changes `README` and `secrets.env` produces stdout with no NUL, so `names.paths()` returns one record like `"README\nsecrets.env\n"` rather than two paths. `changed` is therefore not a list of real paths; subsequent `inside`/scan decisions see a path that matches no actual file and can either wrongly refuse a valid multi-file return or fail to see a real path that must stay home.

chunk_findings.detail: The parametrization deleted the `"."` and `"../.."` cases. `R._safe` is used to build Git ref name components for item/lane identifiers; if `_safe(".")` now returns `"."` or `_safe("../..")` now returns a string containing `..`, this test still passes, and `build_outbound` can then produce an invalid ref such as `refs/heads/swarm/remote/./l`. The removed cases were the only coverage that would catch that regression.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_safe_name_is_one_harmless_component

chunk_findings.detail: The parametrization removed the embedded-slash name `"a/b"` and the empty name `""`, leaving only `"../x"`, `".hidden"`, and `"-f"`. chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_file_names_are_plain

chunk_findings.detail: The new collision-avoidance claim is false because the digest is appended only to names that changed or end in `.lock`, while a safe name equal to that exact output is returned unchanged. Let `h = hashlib.sha256(b"foo.lock").hexdigest()[:8]`. `_safe("foo.lock")` returns `foo.lock-<h>` because it ends in `.lock`. But `_safe(f"foo.lock-{h}")` sees a harmless component not ending in `.lock` and returns it unchanged. Two distinct lane names therefore map to the same path/ref component, so two lanes can share storage or a ref, contradicting the new docstring's guarantee and defeating the fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_safe

chunk_findings.detail: `_inspect` still calls `git diff --name-only` without `-z` while `_git(..., z=True)` and `.paths()` treat stdout as NUL-separated records. A normal return that changes `foo/bar.py` produces `foo/bar.py\n`; with no NUL, `paths()` yields `("foo/bar.py\n",)`. Exclusion, glob, and secret-scan lookups then miss the real path, so a seed file that must stay home (or a secret path) can be treated as a different name and land.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:441

chunk_findings.detail: The digest branch is not injective with the early-return branch. Any name `_ID` rewrites is returned as `f"{out}-{sha256(s)[:8]}"`, and that string is itself a fixed point: it is only letters, digits, and `-`, so `_ID.sub` and `strip("-.")` leave it unchanged and it does not end with `.lock`, so the `out == s` path returns it verbatim. Given lane id `-rf`, `strip("-.")` yields `rf` and `_safe("-rf")` is `rf-` plus the first 8 hex digits of `sha256("-rf")`. A second lane whose id is exactly that string gets the same component. Those two lanes then share one host ref and path segment, which is the collision the digest was added to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_safe

chunk_findings.detail: `test_returned_unscanned_file_is_reported` locks in `import_return` success (`got.ok`, branch kept) when a returned blob is over `scan_max_blob_bytes` and only listed in `unscanned`. Outbound refuses the same situation unless consent sets `unscanned_seen` (`test_file_too_big_to_scan_needs_consent_that_saw_it`), and a scanned secret is a hard fail (`test_returned_secret_is_refused`, empty branch). Given a return of `src/k.py` whose body is `FAKE_KEY` padded past `scan_max_blob_bytes`, the scan skips the blob, `ok` stays true, and the key is committed on `swarm/remote/...`. An untrusted lane bypasses the secret gate by exceeding the scan cap.

chunk_findings.detail: The delta after triage does not alter `_inspect`; the only nearby logic change in `import_return` (`if not got.ok: return got`) is semantically identical to the old `if got.ok: _land ...` fall-through used for failures. The prior confirmed defect therefore still holds: `ok` ignores `unscanned`. A returned branch adding a 2,000,000-byte `big.bin` whose secret starts after the first 1,000,000 bytes makes `_scan` return `hits=[]`, `unscanned=("big.bin",)`, and no `bad`; `_inspect` still returns `ok=True`, and `import_return` still calls `_land` to create the host branch containing the unscanned file, despite the new comment claiming such files are “refused too”.

chunk_findings.detail: The added assertion `git(repo, "for-each-ref", "refs/heads/swarm") == ""` does not match descendant refs such as `refs/heads/swarm/remote/X-1/l`; a no-glob `git for-each-ref` pattern is matched exactly, not as a prefix. A regression that leaves the refused return's branch under `refs/heads/swarm/...` would still return empty output, so the test would pass despite the leaked ref. Previous finding 5 is therefore not answered: the test should query `refs/heads/swarm/*` (or assert the exact branch is absent).

chunk_findings.detail: The test still checks only `"refs/ddflow/remote/" not in git(repo, "for-each-ref")`; a secret-bearing return that leaves `refs/heads/swarm/remote/X-1/l` passes that check because the branch lives under `refs/heads/swarm`. The new `refs/heads/swarm` assertion in `test_returned_file_too_big_to_scan_is_refused` covers only the too-big return, not this test’s secret-bearing refusal path, so previous finding 5 remains.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_refused_return_keeps_no_ref

chunk_findings.detail: The parametrization was narrowed from `["../x", "a/b", ".hidden", "-f", ""]` to `["../x", ".hidden", "-f"]`. That test is the guard that remote file names passed to `SshTransport.copy_out` are plain base names, and `a/b` and `""` are the two cases that catch a path separator and an empty name. After this change, a regression where `copy_out("l", "a/b", tmp_path / "g", 10)` is accepted and reads `a/b` from the lane root, or `copy_out("l", "", tmp_path / "g", 10)` is accepted and passes an empty remote filename, would leave the suite green. The delta claims tests were tightened, but this is a loosening.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_file_names_are_plain

chunk_findings.detail: `_inspect` still passes `z=True` into the result parser but the `git diff --name-only` invocation no longer passes `-z`. `z=True` splits on NUL (that is why the old call passed both). With only newline-separated output, a return that touches more than one path is one record, e.g. `a.txt\nb.txt\n` (and `core.quotepath` wraps `my file.py` in quotes). `changed` is then not the real paths, so excluded-path, glob, and secret checks run against a name that is not in the tree. A lane that edits `README` and `.env` can miss `.env` entirely and still be treated as a clean change set.

chunk_findings.detail: The change replaces the assertion that `cleanup("..")` returns ok and leaves `keep/f` untouched with only `pytest.raises(R.RemoteError)`. A bug where `cleanup("..")` first deletes `(home / k.lanes_root / "keep" / "f")` (or the whole lane parent) and then raises `RemoteError` now passes, so the refusal no longer proves non-destructive traversal is blocked.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:623

chunk_findings.detail: The test still only checks `not hasattr(got.proposals[0], "approved")`; the untrusted second proposal is the one containing `"approved": True`. A parser that preserves an `approved` attribute on `got.proposals[1]` still passes this test, so the invariant “proposals are data never approvals” is not enforced. This diff does not alter the assertion.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::test_proposals_are_data_never_approvals

chunk_findings.detail: The AST walk still collects only `ast.ImportFrom` nodes; a plain `import ddflow.services.events` or `import ddflow.api` is an `ast.Import` node and is omitted from `mods`. The structural guarantee is therefore still not enforced for plain imports, and this diff only changes the docstring.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py::test_module_cannot_write_the_log_or_answer_a_gate

chunk_findings.detail: When `_land` restores the files excluded from the seed pack, it builds `back` lines as `f"{m} {sha}\t{path}"` and feeds them to `git update-index --index-info`. That input format requires `mode SP type SP sha TAB path`; the generated lines omit the object type (`blob`/`commit`). For example, with the default exclusion `.env`, `_land` will invoke `git update-index --index-info` with a line like `100644 <sha>\t.env`; git refuses it as a bad input line. Since this happens after `import_return` fetched and inspected a valid returned lane, any repo whose base commit contains an excluded file (including the default `.env`) cannot import a remote return.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_land

chunk_findings.detail: `build_outbound` never makes `dest` absolute. `G.run(repo, ...)` runs git in the repository directory, so a relative `dest` is interpreted relative to `repo`, while the Python `Path(dest)` operations later read/write relative to the caller’s current directory. For example, `build_outbound(Path('repo'), ..., dest=Path('out'))` causes git to create `repo/out/base.bundle`, but `bundle.stat()` looks for `out/base.bundle` in the current directory; it raises `FileNotFoundError` inside the try block, deletes the ref, and fails the outbound, even when the actual bundle is built successfully.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:build_outbound

chunk_findings.detail: The raw JSON includes a second proposal object with `"approved": True`, but the only approval-related assertion is `not hasattr(got.proposals[0], "approved")`, which inspects the first proposal — the one entry that never had an `approved` key. If `R.parse_proposals` retained an `approved` attribute on the second proposal, this test would still pass, so it does not actually verify the test’s stated property.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_proposals_are_data_never_approvals

chunk_findings.detail: The AST scan only walks `ast.ImportFrom` nodes and ignores `ast.Import` nodes. A plain import such as `import ddflow.gate` or `import ddflow.services.lifecycle` in `remote.py` would not be appended to `mods`, so every `assert not [m for m in mods if word in m]` would still pass even though the module imports a prohibited subsystem.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_module_cannot_write_the_log_or_answer_a_gate

chunk_findings.detail: The call was changed from `_git(..., "-z", out.root, tip, z=True)` to `_git(..., out.root, tip, z=True)`. `z=True` makes `_git` parse stdout as NUL-separated records, but the `git diff` invocation no longer passes `-z`, so Git emits newline-separated paths. With a normal returned change like `foo/bar.py`, stdout is `foo/bar.py\n`, no NUL is present, and `names.paths()` yields `("foo/bar.py\n",)` instead of `("foo/bar.py",)`. This corrupts the changed-file list for every non-empty valid return.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:443

chunk_findings.detail:
In the `via="bundle"` path, the test builds `ret.bundle` from the deliberately malformed `work` branch **before** calling `R.import_return`:

```
git(w, "bundle", "create", "-q", str(src), "work")
```

The `work` branch points at a commit whose tree was created raw with `git hash-object -t tree --stdin` precisely so that Git itself considers it malformed. `git bundle create` must invoke `rev-list --objects`/`pack-objects` and parse that tree to pack the objects; parsing the malformed tree aborts with a fatal error. The `git` test helper raises `CalledProcessError`, so the test terminates before reaching `with pytest.raises(R.RemoteError)`. The bundle import path is therefore never exercised, and the new parametrized case ERRORS/fails instead of testing that `import_return` refuses a malicious return bundle containing this malformed tree.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_malformed_tree_never_lands (via="bundle")

chunk_findings.detail: A return whose tip is clean still keeps secret blobs reachable on the host. Given seed `root`, commit A adding `leak.txt` with a matched secret, and commit B deleting `leak.txt` while changing `README`, `_inspect` only scans tip paths in `changed` (`README`). `hits` is empty, `ok` is true, `_land` writes `refs/heads/swarm/remote/...`, and `refs/ddflow/remote/<item>/<lane>` is left pointing at B, whose parent still holds the secret. The same gap lands a changed file larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes`: it is appended to `unscanned`, not `hits`, so `ok` stays true and the unscanned blob is committed on the host branch. Outbound refuses that case unless consent recorded `unscanned_seen`; inbound does not.
chunk_findings.title: `import_return` / `_inspect` / `_scan`

chunk_findings.detail: The return bundle is created with a relative `git bundle create` after the agent runs, and failure is discarded. The script does `cd work`, then `{agent}`, then `git bundle create -q ../return.bundle {root}..lane >&2 || :`. If the agent exits from `work/pkg` (a normal `cd`), the bundle is written to `work/return.bundle` or a different repo, while `collect` only reads `ddflow-lanes/<lane>/return.bundle`. If create fails in place (disk, missing base, too large), `|| :` still exits with the agent's status, so the host records success and imports nothing.
chunk_findings.title: `lane_argv`

chunk_findings.detail: `STUB` ends with `exec sh -c "$*"`, which joins every remote argv with spaces and re-parses that string as a shell. `test_argv_reaches_the_lane_as_words_not_shell` starts `("sh", "-c", 'printf %s "$1" > out', "x", "a b; touch pwned")`. A transport that execs those as distinct ssh arguments still has the stub run an unquoted `; touch pwned`, so the assertion that `pwned` is absent fails against a correct non-shell transport and does not prove the product avoided a shell.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:STUB

chunk_findings.detail: Return of a blob larger than `scan_max_blob_bytes` is required to be `ok` and is only listed on `unscanned`, then stored on the host branch. A lane that returns `src/k.py` of 101 bytes containing `FAKE_KEY` with `scan_max_blob_bytes=100` therefore skips the secret refusal in `test_returned_secret_is_refused` (and the outbound consent gate for the same unscanned condition) and the key lands under `refs/heads/swarm/remote/...`.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_returned_unscanned_file_is_reported

chunk_findings.detail: The return-path name list dropped git’s `-z` but still asks `_git` for NUL records (`z=True`) and splits with `.paths()`. Every other call in this file that used `.paths()` passed both. `git diff --name-only` without `-z` emits LF-separated, C-quoted names, so a return that touches `README` and `secrets.env` is one blob `README\nsecrets.env` (and a non-UTF-8 excluded name stays quoted). The exclusion gate then never sees the real path, so a seed file that must stay home can ride back in the return branch.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:440

chunk_findings.detail: `forget` now drops only `out.ref`. In any repository that already contains a lane imported by the previous version, a successful `import_return` left `refs/ddflow/remote/<item>/<lane>` pointing at the lane’s unscanned tip. After this change, `forget` no longer deletes that ref, so those pre-existing leaked refs — and any secrets in their histories — remain reachable forever. The new `import_return` fixes future returns via the `finally` deletion of `dest`, but it does not remove old refs created before this delta, and `forget` is the only cleanup path that previously did.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:forget

chunk_findings.detail: The new `names = _git(repo, k, "diff", "--name-only", "--no-renames", out.root, tip, z=True)` drops `-z` from the `git diff` arguments while still setting `z=True`. `_git` will parse stdout as NUL-separated records, but Git emits LF-separated (and C-quoted) names without `-z`. A returned branch that changes `README` and `secrets.env` produces stdout with no NUL, so `names.paths()` returns one record like `"README\nsecrets.env\n"` rather than two paths. `changed` is therefore not a list of real paths; subsequent `inside`/scan decisions see a path that matches no actual file and can either wrongly refuse a valid multi-file return or fail to see a real path that must stay home.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:441

chunk_findings.detail: The parametrization deleted the `"."` and `"../.."` cases. `R._safe` is used to build Git ref name components for item/lane identifiers; if `_safe(".")` now returns `"."` or `_safe("../..")` now returns a string containing `..`, this test still passes, and `build_outbound` can then produce an invalid ref such as `refs/heads/swarm/remote/./l`. The removed cases were the only coverage that would catch that regression.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_safe_name_is_one_harmless_component

chunk_findings.detail: The parametrization removed the embedded-slash name `"a/b"` and the empty name `""`, leaving only `"../x"`, `".hidden"`, and `"-f"`. A transport that starts accepting a remote path such as `a/b` (or an empty name) would no longer fail this regression test, so the test no longer verifies the `file_names_are_plain` property it exists to enforce.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_file_names_are_plain

chunk_findings.detail: The new collision-avoidance claim is false because the digest is appended only to names that changed or end in `.lock`, while a safe name equal to that exact output is returned unchanged. Let `h = hashlib.sha256(b"foo.lock").hexdigest()[:8]`. `_safe("foo.lock")` returns `foo.lock-<h>` because it ends in `.lock`. But `_safe(f"foo.lock-{h}")` sees a harmless component not ending in `.lock` and returns it unchanged. Two distinct lane names therefore map to the same path/ref component, so two lanes can share storage or a ref, contradicting the new docstring's guarantee and defeating the fix.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_safe

chunk_findings.detail: `_inspect` still calls `git diff --name-only` without `-z` while `_git(..., z=True)` and `.paths()` treat stdout as NUL-separated records. A normal return that changes `foo/bar.py` produces `foo/bar.py\n`; with no NUL, `paths()` yields `("foo/bar.py\n",)`. Exclusion, glob, and secret-scan lookups then miss the real path, so a seed file that must stay home (or a secret path) can be treated as a different name and land.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:441

chunk_findings.detail: The digest branch is not injective with the early-return branch. Any name `_ID` rewrites is returned as `f"{out}-{sha256(s)[:8]}"`, and that string is itself a fixed point: it is only letters, digits, and `-`, so `_ID.sub` and `strip("-.")` leave it unchanged and it does not end with `.lock`, so the `out == s` path returns it verbatim. Given lane id `-rf`, `strip("-.")` yields `rf` and `_safe("-rf")` is `rf-` plus the first 8 hex digits of `sha256("-rf")`. A second lane whose id is exactly that string gets the same component. Those two lanes then share one host ref and path segment, which is the collision the digest was added to prevent.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_safe

chunk_findings.detail: `_file` now calls `_safe(name)`, and `_safe` rejects any name ending `.lock` because `.lock` is unsafe as a Git ref component. But `_file` is constructing a filesystem path under a lane directory, not a ref. `_FILE.fullmatch` allows ordinary lockfile names such as `yarn.lock`, `poetry.lock`, `Cargo.lock`, and the old `_file` accepted them; now a lane that returns a changed `yarn.lock` gets `RemoteError("'yarn.lock' is not one plain name")` and the return is refused. This is a regression for common returned lockfiles.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_file

chunk_findings.detail: The previous confirmed finding still holds: no hunk in this delta touches `build_outbound`. `build_outbound(Path('repo'), ..., dest=Path('out'))` still has `G.run(repo, ...)` write `repo/out/base.bundle`, while the later Python `Path(dest)` operations read `out/base.bundle` relative to the caller’s cwd, so the bundle is not found. chunk_findings.detail: The previous confirmed finding still holds: the delta does not change `_inspect`/`_scan`/`_land`. chunk_findings.detail: The previous confirmed finding still holds: oversized blobs are still reported as `unscanned` but allowed. chunk_findings.detail: `_ALIVE` treats any live `lane.pid` with an empty `lane.rc` as the lane, and `signal`/`cleanup` run `kill -s SIG -- "-$(cat lane.pid)"` with no check that the file is the pid this host started. That contradicts the comment that a recycled pid never reads as running: the guarantee holds only if the wrapper lived long enough to write `lane.rc`. If the lane is SIGKILLed or crashes after `echo $! > lane.pid` and before `echo $? > lane.rc`, a later reuse of that pid (or a truncated pid file whose contents are `1`) makes `observe` return `running` and makes `signal`/`cleanup` deliver the signal to that other process group. `kill -- -1` signals every process the ssh user may signal, not the lane.

chunk_findings.detail: `_ALIVE` is false as soon as `lane.rc` is non-empty, so a still-running lane is never checked with `kill -0`. An untrusted agent in `work/` can `echo 0 > ../lane.rc` and keep running; `observe` returns `LaneStatus("exited", exit_code=0)`. `cleanup` uses the same `_ALIVE` test, so it skips `kill` and only `rm -rf`s the directory while that process is still alive. The host can therefore treat the lane as a clean success and `collect` a `return.bundle` the live agent is still free to rewrite.

chunk_findings.detail: `_blobs` assumes `git cat-file --batch` emits a trailing LF after each blob's content: it advances `i` by `nl + 1 + int(size) + 1`. `git cat-file --batch` emits `<sha> <type> <size>\n<contents>` with no LF separator after `<contents>`. With two or more blobs, after the first record `i` lands one byte into the next header, so that record's SHA is parsed with its leading hex character missing. When a later blob contains a secret, `_scan` does `hits += by_sha[sha]` with the truncated key while `by_sha` has the full SHA, raising an unhandled `KeyError` instead of the promised refusal/`RemoteError` result. For example, a base tree with two blobs where only the second contains a private key makes `build_outbound` crash with a traceback rather than refusing the secret.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:_blobs

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that `remote.py` never “reaches the log, gates or approvals,” but it only checks whether the **names of imported modules** contain `"event"`, `"gate"`, `"approval"`, `"lifecycle"`, or `"ddflow.api"`. A concrete violating implementation such as writing an event-log entry with `Path(".ddflow/events/x.jsonl").write_text(...)` or calling a gate function through an already-imported module would not require any new import whose module name contains those words, so the test would still pass. The test therefore gives false confidence and does not exercise the property stated in its docstring.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_swarm_remote.py:test_module_cannot_write_the_log_or_answer_a_gate

chunk_findings.detail: A pushed source that is a directory is fetched with `git fetch <path> +<srcref>:<dest>` and no isolation from that repository’s own config. `git-upload-pack` runs inside the source repo, so a lane-controlled `uploadpack.packObjectsHook` (or equivalent upload-pack config) executes as the host user before ancestry, secret, or link checks. Concrete input: `import_return(host, "/tmp/lane-repo", out, branch="main")` where that repo’s config sets `uploadpack.packObjectsHook` to a shell command. The bundle-file path does not do this; the repository path the function explicitly accepts does. `transfer.fsckObjects` and `GIT_ALLOW_PROTOCOL=file` do not disable hooks in the source repo.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/swarm/remote.py:import_return

chunk_findings.detail: Refusal only inspects the tip tree, then `update-ref -d` drops the fetch ref. chunk_findings.detail: `_blobs` assumes `git cat-file --batch` emits a trailing LF after each blob's content: it advances `i` by `nl + 1 + int(size) + 1`. `git cat-file --batch` emits `<sha> <type> <size>\n<contents>` with no LF separator after `<contents>`. With two or more blobs, after the first record `i` lands one byte into the next header, so that record's SHA is parsed with its leading hex character missing. When a later blob contains a secret, `_scan` does `hits += by_sha[sha]` with the truncated key while `by_sha` has the full SHA, raising an unhandled `KeyError` instead of the promised refusal/`RemoteError` result. For example, a base tree with two blobs where only the second contains a private key makes `build_outbound` crash with a traceback rather than refusing the secret.

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that `remote.py` never “reaches the log, gates or approvals,” but it only checks whether the **names of imported modules** contain `"event"`, `"gate"`, `"approval"`, `"lifecycle"`, or `"ddflow.api"`.
